answers.body:
**Question:** Create a Pod with two containers, both with image busybox and command "echo hello; sleep 3600". Connect to the second container and run 'ls'

**Solution:**

The easiest way to do it is create a pod with a single container and save its definition in a YAML file:

```bash
kubectl run busybox --image=busybox --restart=Never -o yaml --dry-run=client -- /bin/sh -c 'echo hello;sleep 3600' > pod.yaml
vi pod.yaml
```

Copy/paste the container related values, so your final YAML should contain the following two containers (make sure those containers have a different name):

```YAML
containers:
  - args:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    - echo hello;sleep 3600
    image: busybox
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: busybox
    resources: {}
  - args:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    - echo hello;sleep 3600
    image: busybox
    name: busybox2
```

```bash
kubectl create -f pod.yaml
# step: connect to the busybox2 container within the pod
kubectl exec -it busybox -c busybox2 -- /bin/sh
ls
exit

# or
kubectl exec -it busybox -c busybox2 -- ls

# note: you can do some cleanup
kubectl delete po busybox
```

---

checks.label: A pod with two containers exists
Both containers use the busybox image

answers.body:
**Question:** Create a pod with an nginx container exposed on port 80. Add a busybox init container which downloads a page using 'echo "Test" > /work-dir/index.html'. Make a volume of type emptyDir and mount it in both containers. For the nginx container, mount it on "/usr/share/nginx/html" and for the initcontainer, mount it on "/work-dir". When done, get the IP of the created pod and create a busybox pod and run "wget -O- IP"

**Solution:**

The easiest way to do it is create a pod with a single container and save its definition in a YAML file:

```bash
kubectl run box --image=nginx --restart=Never --port=80 --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod-init.yaml
```

Copy/paste the container related values, so your final YAML should contain the volume and the initContainer:

Volume:

```YAML
containers:
- image: nginx
...
  volumeMounts:
  - name: vol
    mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
volumes:
- name: vol
  emptyDir: {}
```

initContainer:

```YAML
...
initContainers:
- args:
  - /bin/sh
  - -c
  - echo "Test" > /work-dir/index.html
  image: busybox
  name: box
  volumeMounts:
  - name: vol
    mountPath: /work-dir
```

In total you get:

```YAML

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    run: box
  name: box
spec:
  initContainers: 
  - args: 
    - /bin/sh 
    - -c 
    - echo "Test" > /work-dir/index.html
    image: busybox 
    name: box 
    volumeMounts: 
    - name: vol 
      mountPath: /work-dir 
  containers:
  - image: nginx
    name: nginx
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
    volumeMounts: 
    - name: vol 
      mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html 
  volumes: 
  - name: vol 
    emptyDir: {} 
```

```bash
# step: apply pod
kubectl apply -f pod-init.yaml

# step: get IP
kubectl get po -o wide

# step: execute wget
kubectl run box-test --image=busybox --restart=Never -it --rm -- /bin/sh -c "wget -O- $(kubectl get pod box -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}')"

# note: you can do some cleanup
kubectl delete po box
```

---

checks.label: Init container mounts the volume at /work-dir
Reached the pod with wget from a busybox pod

answers.body:
**Question:** Create a Pod with two init containers that run in order.

**Solution:**

Init containers run sequentially, each to completion, before the main containers start.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: multi-init
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: work
      emptyDir: {}
  initContainers:
    - name: init-1
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo one > /work/out.txt"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: work
          mountPath: /work
    - name: init-2
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo two >> /work/out.txt"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: work
          mountPath: /work
  containers:
    - name: main
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "cat /work/out.txt; sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: work
          mountPath: /work
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f multi-init.yaml
kubectl logs multi-init            # -> one / two
```

---

checks.label: Main container reads the shared file
checks.name: multi-init

answers.body:
**Question:** Add a native sidecar that tails the app log.

**Solution:**

A native sidecar is an initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always`.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sidecar-log
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: logs
      emptyDir: {}
  initContainers:
    - name: logger
      image: busybox
      restartPolicy: Always
      command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/app.log"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do echo \"$(date) hit\" >> /var/log/app.log; sleep 2; done"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f sidecar-log.yaml
kubectl logs sidecar-log -c logger
```

---

checks.label: Sidecar is an initContainer with restartPolicy Always
checks.name: sidecar-log

**Question:** Ambassador pattern — proxy container in the same Pod.

**Solution:**

Containers in a Pod share the network namespace, so the app reaches the ambassador over `localhost`.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ambassador-pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    - name: proxy
      image: nginx
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f ambassador-pod.yaml
kubectl exec ambassador-pod -c app -- wget -O- localhost:80
```

---

**Question:** Adapter pattern — sidecar reformats output.

**Solution:**

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: adapter-pod
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: data
      emptyDir: {}
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do echo raw-metric-$(date +%s) >> /data/metrics.log; sleep 3; done"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
    - name: adapter
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /data/metrics.log | while read l; do echo formatted:$l; done"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f adapter-pod.yaml
kubectl logs adapter-pod -c adapter
```

---

**Question:** Share an in-memory emptyDir between two containers.

**Solution:**

`medium: Memory` backs the emptyDir with a tmpfs.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: mem-cache
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: cache
      emptyDir:
        medium: Memory
  containers:
    - name: writer
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /cache
    - name: reader
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /cache
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f mem-cache.yaml
kubectl exec mem-cache -c writer -- sh -c 'echo hi > /cache/data'
kubectl exec mem-cache -c reader -- cat /cache/data
```

---

checks.label: Cache mounted in both containers at /cache
checks.name: mem-cache

**Question:** Enable a shared process namespace in a Pod.

**Solution:**

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: shared-ns
spec:
  shareProcessNamespace: true
  containers:
    - name: c1
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    - name: c2
      image: busybox
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f shared-ns.yaml
kubectl exec shared-ns -c c1 -- ps aux   # sees c2's sleep too
```

---
